Mammoth is a beginner-friendly language for the JVM. It compiles `.mam` files directly to JVM bytecode, and it can call Java libraries: the JDK, Minecraft's Fabric API, or a JAR on your `CLASSPATH`.

> **Status: experimental preview (0.1.0).** The language, its standard library and the compiler's error messages may change between releases without a migration path. The test suites run on Windows with Java 17. Linux and macOS have not been tested. Java interop covers the cases the tests exercise and is not complete; see [Java generic assignment safety and current limits](./performance-measurements/#java-generic-assignment-safety-and-current-limits). Known open issues are listed in [docs/development/HANDOFF.md](https://github.com/evilstdio/Mammoth/blob/main/docs/development/HANDOFF.md).

```mammoth
fun greet(name: Text) {
    print("Hello, {name}!")
}

for name in ["Maya", "Sam"] {
    greet(name)
}
```
